title_en: A verb and its little word: one unit
q_en: Which little word does this verb take, and does it change the meaning?
q_ar: أَيُّ حَرْفٍ يَأْتِي مَعَ هَذَا الْفِعْلِ؟ وَهَلْ يُغَيِّرُ الْمَعْنَى؟
not_yet: Every verb with every little word: you learn them one by one, by reading.
Why Arabic chooses one little word and not another: it is the habit of the language, not a rule to work out.
The little word before a verb (“to do”): Lesson 69.
not_yet_ar: كُلُّ فِعْلٍ مَعَ كُلِّ حَرْفٍ: تَتَعَلَّمُهَا وَاحِدًا وَاحِدًا بِالْقِرَاءَةِ.
لِمَاذَا تَخْتَارُ الْعَرَبِيَّةُ حَرْفًا دُونَ آخَرَ: هَذِهِ عَادَةُ اللُّغَةِ، لَا قَاعِدَةٌ تُسْتَنْتَجُ.
الْحَرْفُ قَبْلَ الْفِعْلِ («أَنْ تَفْعَلَ»): فِي الدَّرْسِ ٦٩.

lines: Sentences 1 and 2 use the same verb. What is different? What happens to the meaning?
الْجُمْلَتَانِ ١ وَ٢ فِيهِمَا الْفِعْلُ نَفْسُهُ. مَا الْمُخْتَلِفُ؟ مَاذَا حَدَثَ لِلْمَعْنَى؟

مَاذَا يَأْتِي بَعْدَ الْحَرْفِ: اسْمٌ مَكْسُورٌ، أَمْ ضَمِيرٌ مِثْلُ ـهِ؟

slides.head_en: Look: a ḥadīth made of little words

lines: عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ ﷺ قَالَ
From Abū Hurayra: the Messenger of God, peace and blessings upon him, said:
مَنْ دَعَا إِلَى هُدًى كَانَ لَهُ مِنَ الْأَجْرِ مِثْلُ أُجُورِ مَنْ تَبِعَهُ
"Whoever calls to guidance will have a reward like the rewards of those who follow him,
لَا يَنْقُصُ ذَلِكَ مِنْ أُجُورِهِمْ شَيْئًا
without that diminishing their rewards in the least.

sections.name: A
sections.en: Counsel from Imam al-Ḥaddād. Read it aloud, then answer.
lines: وَهَذَا التَّفَكُّرُ يُثْمِرُ لَكَ الزُّهْدَ فِي الدُّنْيَا وَالرَّغْبَةَ فِي الْآخِرَةِ
And this reflection bears for you detachment from this world and desire for the next.
And you should give up joking altogether.
حَمَلَنِي عَلَى وَضْعِهَا الِامْتِثَالُ لِأَمْرِ اللهِ تَعَالَى وَأَمْرِ رَسُولِهِ ، وَالرَّغْبَةُ فِي الْوَعْدِ الصَّادِقِ
What moved me to write it was obedience to the command of God Most High and of His messenger, and desire for the true promise.
sections.cite: al-Ḥaddād, Risālat al-Muʿāwana wa-l-Muẓāhara wa-l-Muʾāzara (Silsilat kutub al-Imām al-Ḥaddād, no. 3), Dār al-Ḥāwī li-l-Ṭibāʿa wa-l-Nashr wa-l-Tawzīʿ, 2nd ed., 1414 AH (title page of the Shamela text); Master Library copy (Bafaqih 22222 install, 241.mdb), pp. 14–147 of the digital text (the copy opens the text at p. 13, which suggests it follows the print; not checked against a print). Three sentences (nos. 1, 3 and 4 of the four in the research file); vowels added by the course (vowelled for learners).

items.en: Line 3: what two things moved the writer to write? Find the two nouns.

items.model: Obedience (الِامْتِثَالُ) to the command of God and His messenger, and desire (الرَّغْبَةُ) for the promise.

items.en: Find the word that means “desire”. What does it have in common with the verb رَغِبَ?
items.ar_q: جِدِ الْكَلِمَةَ الَّتِي تَعْنِي «الْمَيْلَ إِلَى الشَّيْءِ». مَا الَّذِي تَشْتَرِكُ فِيهِ مَعَ رَغِبَ؟
items.model: الرَّغْبَةُ. Both come from the root ر غ ب, and both take فِي for “desire for”.

items.en: Who is the writer speaking to in lines 1 and 2? How do you know?
items.ar_q: إِلَى مَنْ يَتَكَلَّمُ الْكَاتِبُ فِي السَّطْرَيْنِ؟ كَيْفَ عَرَفْتَ؟
options: And you should give up joking altogether.
To “you”: the endings ـكَ in لَكَ and عَلَيْكَ.
items.answer: To “you”: the endings ـكَ in لَكَ and عَلَيْكَ.
items.model: To “you”: the endings ـكَ in لَكَ and عَلَيْكَ.

items.en: ★ Here الرَّغْبَةُ is “desire for”. What would رَغْبَةٌ عَنْ mean, and why would it not fit?
items.ar_q: ★ مَاذَا تَعْنِي «رَغْبَةٌ عَنْ»؟ وَلِمَاذَا لَا تُنَاسِبُ هُنَا؟
items.model: “Turning away from”. It would say the writer turns away from the true promise, the opposite of what he means.

items.en: ★ The writer gives his reasons for writing (line 3). Why would a teacher begin a book of advice with his reasons?
items.ar_q: ★ لِمَاذَا يَبْدَأُ الْمُعَلِّمُ كِتَابَ النَّصِيحَةِ بِذِكْرِ أَسْبَابِهِ؟
items.model: He shows that he writes to obey God and to win the promise, not to show off. The reader then reads the advice in the right spirit.

sections.name: B
sections.en: A short text: the saying of the Habib. Read it aloud, then answer.
lines: فِي الْمَسَاءِ جَلَسَ أَحْمَدُ مَعَ عُمَرَ فِي حَلْقَةِ الْحَبِيبِ.
In the evening Ahmad sat with Umar in the Habib’s circle.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: رَغِبَ بَعْضُ النَّاسِ فِي الْمَالِ، وَرَغِبَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَالِ.
The Habib said: Some people desired wealth, and some of them turned away from wealth.
ثُمَّ سَأَلَ أَحْمَدُ: لِمَاذَا رَغِبَ بَعْضُهُمْ عَنِ الْمَالِ؟
Then Ahmad asked: Why did some of them turn away from wealth?
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: لِأَنَّهُمْ نَظَرُوا إِلَى الْآخِرَةِ وَرَغِبُوا فِيهَا.
The Habib said: Because they looked to the Hereafter and desired it.
وَقَالَ عُمَرُ: أَنَا أَرْغَبُ فِي الْعِلْمِ.
And Umar said: I desire knowledge.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ: اُطْلُبِ الْعِلْمَ، وَلَا تَرْغَبْ عَنِ الْمَجْلِسِ.
The Habib said: Seek knowledge, and do not turn away from the majlis.
رَجَعَ أَحْمَدُ إِلَى الْبَيْتِ وَقَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: أَنَا أَرْغَبُ فِي الْعِلْمِ.
Ahmad returned to the house and said to his mother: I desire knowledge.
وَدَعَا الْحَبِيبُ لَهُ: دَعَوْتُ لَكَ يَا أَحْمَدُ.
And the Habib prayed for him: I have prayed for you, Ahmad.

sections.name: K
sections.en: Translate the two lines: the second half of the ḥadīth. It is built like the first half you read.
lines: وَمَنْ دَعَا إِلَى ضَلَالَةٍ كَانَ عَلَيْهِ مِنَ الْإِثْمِ مِثْلُ آثَامِ مَنْ تَبِعَهُ
And whoever calls to misguidance will bear a sin like the sins of those who follow him,
لَا يَنْقُصُ ذَلِكَ مِنْ آثَامِهِمْ شَيْئًا
without that diminishing their sins in the least."
sections.cite: Muslim, al-Jāmiʿ al-Ṣaḥīḥ, Dār al-Jīl (Beirut) / Dār al-Āfāq al-Jadīda print (Shamela 1786, vowelled, matches the print), vol. 8 p. 62; Muḥammad Fuʾād ʿAbd al-Bāqī numbering (Shamela 1785, Dār Iḥyāʾ al-Turāth al-ʿArabī): 4/2060; already verified in Hadith_Compendium (hub hadith muslim 2674). Ḥadīth text as in the vowelled print; the salutation is vowelled by the course (vowelled for learners).

items.model: And whoever calls to misguidance will bear a sin like the sins of those who follow him, without that diminishing their sins in the least.

sections.name: L
sections.en: Translate the sentence: counsel from Imam al-Ḥaddād about calling, pointing and advising.
lines: الَّذِي جَعَلَ الدَّعْوَةَ إِلَى الْهُدَى ، وَالدَّلَالَةَ عَلَى الْخَيْرِ ، وَالنَّصِيحَةَ لِلْمُسْلِمِينَ ، مِنْ أَفْضَلِ الْقُرُبَاتِ
He who made calling to guidance, pointing to good, and sincere counsel for the Muslims among the best of the acts that bring one near.
sections.cite: al-Ḥaddād, al-Naṣāʾiḥ al-Dīniyya wa-l-Waṣāyā al-Īmāniyya (Silsilat kutub al-Imām al-Ḥaddād, no. 1), Dār al-Ḥāwī, 1st ed. 1413, 2nd ed. 1418 AH (title page of the Shamela text); Master Library copy (Bafaqih 22222 install, 1416.mdb), p. 23 of the digital text (opens at p. 23, which suggests print pagination; not checked against a print). sections.name: N
sections.en: Find the mistake.

items.en: A student translates: “Ahmad desired knowledge.” What is wrong?
items.model: With عَنْ the verb means “turned away from”. The sentence says: Ahmad turned away from knowledge. For “desired” the sentence needs فِي.

items.en: What is wrong with the ending?
items.model: After the little word فِي the noun must end in kasra: فِي الْعِلْمِ.

items.en: A student means “the boy prayed for his father”. What is wrong?
items.model: إِلَى means “to, towards”: he called to his father. For “prayed for” use لِـ: دَعَا لِأَبِيهِ.

items.en: A student means “the student read in the book”. What is wrong?
items.model: قَرَأَ عَلَى is for reading to a person (a teacher). For a book use فِي: قَرَأَ فِي الْكِتَابِ.

sections.name: Y
sections.en: The Story Strip: lines 1–116
lines: A boy went to a mosque.
The boy sat in the mosque.
The boy opened a muṣḥaf (a copy of the Qur’an).
The boy read in the muṣḥaf.
The boy sat in the study circle.
The friends went to the mosque.
The students read in the books.
The Habib sat in the mosque.
The Habib is a righteous man.
Is the Habib in the mosque?
Yes, the Habib is in the mosque.
The boy came in through the door.
The mother looked at the boy.
The boy sits in the study circle today.
Maryam is reading the muṣḥaf now.
The boy was happy in the majlis.
Maryam was happy in the study circle.
The boy did not leave the majlis.
لَنْ يَجْلِسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْبَيْتِ غَدًا.
The boy will not sit at home tomorrow.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَبِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ.
The boy went with the father to the ziyāra (the visit).
The boy sat with good manners in the majlis.
The boy heard the Rātib (the litany) with his father.
ذَهَبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ إِلَى بَيْتِ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy went in the morning to the Habib’s house.
The boy sat in the circle of dhikr (remembrance of Allah).
The Habib asked him about the lesson.
The boy served the guests and carried the food.
ثُمَّ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ وَسَمِعَ الدَّرْسَ.
Then the boy sat with the Habib and heard the lesson.
The guests thanked the boy who served them.
حَفِظَ الْوَلَدُ مَا سَمِعَ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ.
The boy memorised what he heard from the Habib.
فَهِمَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ لِأَنَّهُ خَدَمَ الضُّيُوفَ.
The boy understood the lesson because he served the guests.
فِي الْمَجْلِسِ خَمْسَةُ ضُيُوفٍ وَسَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ كُلَّ كَلِمَةٍ.
There are five guests in the majlis, and the boy heard every word.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الرِّبَاطِ فِي الصَّبَاحِ.
The boy came to the ribāṭ in the morning.
The Habib said: Knowledge is light.
سَأَلَ عُمَرُ صَدِيقَهُ: هَلْ أَنْتَ ذَاهِبٌ إِلَى الرَّوْحَةِ؟
Umar asked his friend: Are you going to the rawḥa?
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: الصَّلَاةُ نُورٌ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Prayer is light.
The boy opened his muṣḥaf and read his wird (his daily portion).
صَلَّى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الطُّلَّابِ ثُمَّ دَعَا.
The boy prayed with the students, then made duʿāʾ.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الْمَوْلِدَ لِأَنَّ مَحَبَّةَ النَّبِيِّ ﷺ فِي قَلْبِهِ.
The boy read the mawlid because love of the Prophet ﷺ is in his heart.
قَالَ الْحَبِيبُ لِأَبِي الْوَلَدِ: وَلَدُكَ طَالِبُ عِلْمٍ.
The Habib said to the boy’s father: Your son is a student of knowledge (ṭālib ʿilm).
جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي مَجَالِسِ الْعُلَمَاءِ فِي تَرِيمَ.
The boy sat in the gatherings of the scholars in Tarim.
يُقَالُ إِنَّ الْإِمَامَ وُلِدَ فِي تَرِيمَ.
It is said that the Imam was born in Tarim.
It was said to the boy: Knowledge is light.
عَلَّمَ الْحَبِيبُ الْوَلَدَ: اللَّهُمَّ صَلِّ وَسَلِّمْ عَلَى سَيِّدِنَا مُحَمَّدٍ ﷺ.
The Habib taught the boy: O Allah, bless and grant peace to our master Muḥammad ﷺ.
The boy reminded his friend of the prayer.
فِي اللَّيْلِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْأَصْحَابِ وَقَرَأَ الرَّاتِبَ.
At night the boy sat with the companions and read the Rātib.
قَالُوا: سُبْحَانَ اللَّهِ، وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ، وَاللَّهُ أَكْبَرُ.
They said: Glory be to Allah, and praise be to Allah, and Allah is greater.
فِي لَيْلَةِ الْقَدْرِ جَلَسَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْمَسْجِدِ مَعَ أَبِيهِ.
On the Night of Qadr the boy sat in the mosque with his father.
The boy helped the guests and honoured them.
The students helped one another in the ribāṭ.
The boy was humble and learned from them.
اِنْتَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ الْحَبِيبَ عِنْدَ بَابِ الْمَسْجِدِ.
The boy waited for the Habib at the door of the mosque.
اِجْتَمَعَ الطُّلَّابُ فِي الصَّبَاحِ وَاسْتَمَعَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْحَبِيبِ.
The students gathered in the morning and the boy listened to the Habib.
حَجَّ أَبُو الْوَلَدِ ثُمَّ رَجَعَ مِنْ مَكَّةَ.
The boy’s father made the pilgrimage, then returned from Mecca.
أَخَذَ الْوَلَدُ التَّمْرَ مِنْ أَبِيهِ وَقَدَّمَهُ لِلضُّيُوفِ.
The boy took the dates from his father and offered them to the guests.
The boy heard a ḥadīth with its chain.
قَالَ الرَّاوِي: حَدَّثَنَا وَأَخْبَرَنَا، ثُمَّ قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: إِنَّمَا الْأَعْمَالُ بِالنِّيَّاتِ.
The narrator said: He told us, and he informed us, then the Prophet ﷺ said: Deeds are only by intentions.
سَمِعَ الْوَلَدُ مِنَ الْحَبِيبِ: قَالَ النَّبِيُّ ﷺ: قُلْ آمَنْتُ بِاللَّهِ فَاسْتَقِمْ.
The boy heard from the Habib: The Prophet ﷺ said: Say: I believe in Allah, and then be upright.
The boy stood up and said: I believe in Allah.
مَشَى الْوَلَدُ مَعَ أَبِيهِ إِلَى الزِّيَارَةِ وَوَصَلَ فِي الْمَسَاءِ.
The boy walked with his father to the ziyāra and arrived in the evening.
The boy made duʿāʾ: O Allah, guide us.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَقَالَ: مَا أَحْسَنَ هَذَا الْمَجْلِسَ!
The boy came to the majlis and said: How beautiful this majlis is!
قَالَ لِأُمِّهِ: جِئْتُ إِلَى الْمَجْلِسِ وَرَأَيْتُ الْحَبِيبَ.
He said to his mother: I came to the majlis and I saw the Habib.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ كَلِمَاتٍ مِنْ جَذْرٍ وَاحِدٍ: عَلَّمَ، مُعَلِّمٌ، تَعْلِيمٌ.
The boy wrote words from one root: ʿallama, muʿallim, taʿlīm.
And he wrote: sāfara, musāfir, safar.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى مِنْبَرِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمِحْرَابِهِ.
The boy looked at the minbar of the mosque and its miḥrāb.
قَالَ الْوَلَدُ: أَنَا حَضْرَمِيٌّ مِنْ تَرِيمَ.
The boy said: I am a Ḥaḍramī, from Tarim.
نَظَرَ الْوَلَدُ بِنَفْسِهِ فِي الْمُعْجَمِ وَوَجَدَ مَعْنَى الْكَلِمَةِ.
The boy looked in the dictionary by himself and found the meaning of the word.
ثُمَّ كَتَبَ الْجَذْرَ وَالْمَعْنَى فِي كِتَابِهِ.
Then he wrote the root and the meaning in his book.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ مَعَ الْحَبِيبِ مَتْنًا صَغِيرًا.
The boy read a small matn (a short base text) with the Habib.
أَصْبَحَ الْمَتْنُ سَهْلًا لَكِنَّ الدَّرْسَ طَوِيلٌ.
The matn became easy, but the lesson is long.
جَاءَ الْوَلَدُ إِلَى الدَّرْسِ مُسْرِعًا وَجَلَسَ مُسْتَقْبِلَ الْقِبْلَةِ.
The boy came to the lesson hurrying, and sat facing the qibla.
And the Habib was pleased with him.
ذَكَرَ الْوَلَدُ اللَّهَ كَثِيرًا وَصَلَّى عَلَى النَّبِيِّ ﷺ ثَلَاثًا.
The boy remembered Allah a great deal and prayed for blessings on the Prophet ﷺ three times.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ الدَّرْسَ مَرَّتَيْنِ طَلَبًا لِلْعِلْمِ.
The boy read the lesson twice, seeking knowledge.
The Habib gave the boy a small book.
ظَنَّ الْوَلَدُ الْكِتَابَ صَعْبًا فَقَالَ: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ.
The boy thought the book difficult, so he said: There is no power and no strength except through Allah.
كَتَبَ الْوَلَدُ أَرْكَانَ الْوُضُوءِ: الْأَوَّلُ النِّيَّةُ، وَالثَّانِي غَسْلُ الْوَجْهِ.
The boy wrote the pillars of the ablution: the first, the intention; and the second, washing the face.
وَالثَّالِثُ غَسْلُ الْيَدَيْنِ، وَالرَّابِعُ مَسْحُ بَعْضِ الرَّأْسِ.
And the third, washing the hands; and the fourth, wiping part of the head.
The boy read the wird in the morning.
ثُمَّ دَعَا: يَا رَبِّ، اِهْدِنَا وَاعْفُ عَنَّا، آمِينَ.
Then he made duʿāʾ: O my Lord, guide us and pardon us. Amen.
شَرِبَ الْوَلَدُ مِنْ مَاءِ الْمَسْجِدِ وَمَا شَرِبَ إِلَّا مَاءً طَاهِرًا.
The boy drank from the water of the mosque, and he drank only pure water.
Neither its colour nor its taste had changed.
قَرَأَ الْوَلَدُ اِسْمَ الشَّيْخِ عَلَى الْكِتَابِ: سَالِمُ بْنُ يُوسُفَ.
The boy read the shaykh’s name on the book: Salim son of Yusuf.
And his kunya is Abū Aḥmad.
رَغِبَ الْوَلَدُ فِي الْعِلْمِ وَالْأَجْرِ وَرَغِبَ عَنِ الْإِثْمِ.
The boy desired knowledge and reward, and turned away from sin.
فَقَالَ لَهُ الْحَبِيبُ: لَا تَرْغَبْ فِي الدُّنْيَا.
So the Habib said to him: Do not set your desire on this world.

items.en: Translate the two new lines into English.
items.model: The boy desired knowledge and reward, and turned away from sin. So the Habib said to him: Do not set your desire on this world.

items.en: Which preposition goes with رَغِبَ for “to desire” and which for “to turn away from”?
options: فِي for desire; عَنْ for turning away.
items.answer: فِي for desire; عَنْ for turning away.
items.model: فِي for desire; عَنْ for turning away.

items.en: Which word is the opposite of الْأَجْرِ (reward)?
options: فِي for desire; عَنْ for turning away.

items.en: Write in Arabic: The boy desired knowledge.
options: فِي for desire; عَنْ for turning away.
